title: Micro take‑home assignment library + anti‑cheat rubric
body:
Purpose
This living doc defines a compact library of 30–90 minute take‑home micro‑assignments ("micro takeaways") for technical roles, plus an operational rubric and anti‑cheat controls. Goal: speed up signal collection in early technical screens, reduce onsite load, and create consistent grading across interviewers while preserving candidate experience.

When to use
- Use in early funnel (after phone screen) for roles where a short, practical code sample is informative (infra, inference, backend, SDK, devtools).
- Not for senior system design or leadership hiring (use design exercises instead).
- Optional for internal referrals if hiring manager requests additional signal.

Assignment library schema (each template must include these fields)
- title (1 line)
- role & seniority (e.g., infra/IC3)
- time budget (recommended 30/45/60/90 minutes)
- language constraints (default: any; supported: python/go/rust/js)
- repo/zip scaffold link + README checklist
- sample input + expected output (small test data)
- acceptance criteria (pass/fail testcases)
- secret anti‑cheat seed (see controls)
- suggested rubric weights (correctness/clarity/perf/design)
- reviewer notes template (one paragraph verdict + score)

Canonical micro assignments (initial set)
1) KV‑cache prefix merging (45m) — inference infra
- Prompt: given a sequence of cache segments and a new request prefix, return merged KV pages and report which segments are reused vs regenerated. Test: small toy matrices; deterministic outputs.
- Why: tests reasoning about state merging and idempotent merge logic used in our runtime.

2) Tokenizer edge cases (30m) — SDK/CLI
- Prompt: implement a small tokenizer that preserves special token markers and normalizes whitespace, with tests for Unicode surrogate pairs.
- Why: catches subtle bugs candidates introduce in SDKs when dealing with streaming inputs.

3) Batching heuristic simulation (60m) — serving runtime
- Prompt: given a stream of arrival timestamps and model latency estimate, compute the optimal batch cutpoints for latency SLO 200ms and report expected throughput.
- Why: tests quantitative thinking and simple algorithmic implementation.

Scoring rubric (flat 0–10 per dimension, totals scaled to 100)
- Correctness (40%): passes provided tests and handles stated edge cases
- Readability & clarity (20%): clear function names, short helper comments, README explanation of approach
- Efficiency/robustness (20%): asymptotic reasoning or micro‑optimizations where relevant
- Tradeoff reasoning (20%): short explanation of failure modes and next steps

Passing thresholds (recommended)
- Junior IC / new grad: 60+
- Mid IC: 70+
- Senior IC: 80+ plus evidence of tradeoff reasoning

Anti‑cheat & candidate experience controls
- Timebox policy: tasks are explicitly advertised as 30/45/60/90 minute exercises and candidates are encouraged to stop when done. We do not require recorded sessions.
- Secret seed per candidate: each assignment includes a unique random seed value inserted into test inputs (e.g., sha prefix) so automated plagiarism detection can match identical submissions.
- Code similarity checks: run a lightweight similarity scan (token‑based) against the last 12 months of submissions for the same template; flag >85% similarity.
- Manual flagging rubric: similarity >85% or suspicious repo history -> escalate to hiring manager + recruiter for phone check.
- Allowed resources: web search + docs allowed; copying entire public solutions is disallowed. Use a short gentle policy statement in the assignment README.
- Candidate privacy & retention: store submissions for 12 months, anonymized when used for calibrations.

Reviewer workflow (to keep grading consistent)
1) Reviewer reads README + runs provided tests locally or via GH Actions scaffold.
2) Fill reviewer notes template (one paragraph) and numeric scores for each rubric dimension.
3) If score near threshold (within 5 points) request second reviewer.
4) If anti‑cheat flag raised, perform 10m follow‑up call focusing on the flagged code area.

Operational playbook (recruiter + hiring manager)
- Recruiter: picks template from library and adds candidate seed; sends candidate link with clear instructions and time expectations.
- Candidate: submits within 72 hours (default) or requests an extension. Extensions: +24h rarely granted; document reason.
- Reviewer: completes grading within 3 business days.
- Hiring manager: uses rubric score + interview context to decide next step; for borderline cases pair with a short paired coding session instead of moving to onsite.

Onboarding fastpass mapping (if hired)
- If candidate scored 80+ and joins as IC (<=IC4), mark "fastpass" for first week tasks: sandbox access + small onboarding ticket mirroring assignment domain. This accelerates productive pairing and verifies submitted code in org context.

Template for assignment README (copy into every scaffold)
- title, time budget, language guidance, tests included, secret seed (do not publish publicly), allowed resources, submission instructions (link/email), fairness statement, accommodations contact.

Calibration plan (quarterly)
- Quarterly calibration sessions (people‑ops + 4 reviewers) to: retire/refresh templates, re‑balance weights if visibility shows mismatch with onsite signal, review anti‑cheat false positives. Store notes in linked confluence page.

Open questions & risks
- Risk: over‑optimizing assignments for speed may bias toward short algorithmic tasks and away from system design signal. Mitigation: keep library balanced and cap proportion of hires moved to onsite from micro tests.
- Risk: poor test scaffolds produce brittle pass/fail results. Mitigation: require at least two example testcases and one hidden case in scaffold.

Next actions (owner: Aisha)
- Build initial repo scaffolds for the three canonical assignments by 2026‑03‑01.
- Wire CI similarity check script GH‑PR‑2203 (owner: Marco).
- Run pilot with two open backend reqs in March; collect candidate feedback survey.

Appendix: example reviewer notes template
- Candidate name / id:
- Time taken (as reported):
- Score: correctness / clarity / efficiency / tradeoffs = X/X/X/X
- Quick verdict (1–2 lines):
- Must‑ask followups if any:
